full_judgment: 30. Given the fact that petitioner No. 1 is claiming the transfer of these shares took place immediately prior to the death of the transferor Alhaj Nurul Islam Sarker (his father) on 5-1-2001 and that too also without furnishing a plausible background or necessity of such transactions, this Court sees it as an unusual transaction, inasmuch as in our society a father as a normal course of action world not decide to transfer his entire asset only in favour of one child by depriving his other five children. In other words, the presumption as to taking place of such transfer of shares by the father of petitioner No. 1 to the name of petitioner No. 1 does not go in favour of petitioner No. 1. That is why, it was incumbent upon petitioner No. 1 to endeavour to rebut and overcome the adverse presumption by adducing credible evidence before this Court. Since petitioner No.1 has utterly failed to prove the title of the shares of 1,715 of late Alhaj Nurul Islam Sarker, who is the source of title of shares of 1,715 shares of petitioner No. 1, this Court holds that the share-structure of the Banani Pictures Ltd as was recorded in the company's Members Register before the alleged transfer of shares dated 15-7-2000 being the valid and lawful one, the Members' Register of the company is required to be rectified according to the aforesaid share-structure, which is given below:
